lab_intro: Choose an input, flip a bit, fire a probe and check every value. Everything is computed right now, in your browser, by the same engine the repository tests against Python.
modo_desc_explorar: Narrative and play. Every number has its exact value one click away.
modo_desc_verificar: Hexadecimal values, tables, vectors, export and the command to reproduce. The numbers are the same as in the other mode.
sessao_intro: It starts with the project case: x = 1 against x = 0, y = 2, a demonstration key (bytes 00 to 1f) and session 1. Change anything: nothing leaves your browser.
sessao_editar: Edit x, y, key, session and rounds
sessao_bit_ajuda: 0 to 254 flips a bit of x. 255 to 509 flips a bit of y.
sessao_chave_ajuda: Do not paste a real key. This key exists only for the demonstration and never leaves your browser.
resumo_sessao: x = {x} · y = {y} · session = {n} · {r} rounds · flipped bit #{bit} ({onde})
erro_x: x must be an integer (decimal or 0x…) with 0 ≤ x < 2^255 − 19.
erro_y: y must be an integer (decimal or 0x…) with 0 ≤ y < 2^255 − 19.
erro_n: The session must be an integer with 0 ≤ n < 2^64.
erro_chave: The key must have exactly 64 hexadecimal digits (32 bytes).
erro_rodadas: Rounds must be an integer from 1 to 255.
erro_bit: The flipped bit must be an integer from 0 to 509.
erro_bit_fora: That flipped bit would make x or y reach 2^255 − 19 or more. Choose another bit.
rod_legenda: Position in the grid is just a label: the linear layer mixes all 32 words at once, there is no neighborhood. Rows 0 and 1 = x, rows 2 and 3 = y.
rod_m_saida: Differing bits in the final output
rod_momento_grupo: Choose the moment of the execution
rotulacao_m0: Moment 0: input with the round key rk[0] already added. Here the two executions differ only where the bit was flipped.
origem_m: state after round {r} of the {total}-round execution (execution A)
rot_nota: Round 1 of the {total}-round execution differs in {w8} words and {b8} bits. A reduced instance, computed with rounds = 1 (its own key schedule and domain), differs in {w1} words and {b1} bits. They are different computations: the reduced instance is not the full execution seen halfway. Both stay near half of the 512 bits.
painel_vazio: Choose a block to see every detail of its value.
painel_pos_txt: row {lin}, column {col} of the 4×8 grid (just a label)
painel_xor: Difference from the other execution: 0x{xor} ({n} bits).
conf_rotulo: Check by hand: type the expected value (hex)
conf_ajuda: Up to 4 hexadecimal digits. The laboratory draws the expected block next to the computed one.
conf_igual: They match: the typed value equals the computed one.
conf_invalido: Use 1 to 4 hexadecimal digits (0 to 9 and a to f).
palpite_titulo: Stone in the well: make a guess
palpite_texto: Before looking at the result, bet: after round 1, how many of the 512 bits change because of a single flipped input bit?
palpite_invalido: Type a whole number from 0 to 512.
palpite_resultado: Computed result: {real} bits. Your guess was off by {dif}. Half of the bits would be {meta}.
palpite_hist: Your last {n} guesses were off by {erro} bits on average (stored only in this browser).
palpite_lembrete: Full diffusion in one round is not security: the beam mission below still distinguishes 2 rounds.
exp_texto: Download the full trace of this execution as JSON (states per round, keys, constants, outputs and differences). The laboratory shows the file's SHA-256 so you can check it.
exp_incluir_chave: Include the demonstration key in the file and in the link
exp_reproduzir: To check it in the repository, run:
chaves_intro: Each seal is a 16-bit block, like those of the state. Adding a key is a bitwise XOR: a pixel lights up where the two differ.
chaves_chaveiro_nota: Each cell is one byte (two glyphs, high nibble on the left). The index is k = row × 8 + column.
chaves_selo_nota: Same indexing as the state: word W[k] receives rk[r][k].
rc_nenhum: The initial addition uses only rk[0], with no constant.
rc_texto: rc[{r}] = 0x{hex}, added to all 32 words after the S-box. It is the same in all 32 (this is finding RT-F1-03).
chaves_aviso: In real use the key is never displayed. Showing the bits here does not measure security, and key size is not a security argument.
feixe_intro: The probe does not know the key. It picks one word, runs all 65,536 possible values through it, keeps the other 31 fixed and sums (XOR) the 32 outputs of each. If a word's sum is zero, its well stays still: the structure shows without the key.
feixe_palavra: Word that varies (0 to 15 = x, 16 to 31 = y)
feixe_camara: Sealed chamber: in this mode the key is drawn at random for each shot and only revealed afterwards.
feixe_chave_sessao: In this mode the probe uses the key from the input above.
feixe_mosaico: A 256 by 256 mosaic that lights up as the 65,536 values are processed
feixe_vazio: Choose the word and the rounds and fire the probe.
feixe_pocos: The 32 wells: the sum of each output word
feixe_resumo: Instance of {r} round(s), word {w} varying: {parados} wells still (sum 0) and {ond} rippling.
feixe_tempo: Computed in this browser in {ms} ms.
feixe_chave_usada: Key used: the one from the input.
feixe_distingue_det: 32 of 32 wells still: the structure is visible without knowing the key. In this probe, the defense yields at {r} round(s).
feixe_nao_distingue: The probe does not distinguish ({r} round(s)).
feixe_nao_distingue_det: No well stopped. Other probes exist, this laboratory tests few, and the project has no independent audit: this is not proof of security.
feixe_inesperado_det: {parados} wells stopped, neither all nor none. Note the input and open an issue in the repository.
feixe_erro: The background computation could not run.
feixe_acaso: The chance of one well staying still by accident is 2^-16. For 32 wells to stay still together it is 2^-512. That is why 32 of 32 is a decisive distinguisher, not a coincidence.
feixe_nao_prova_t: What this probe does not prove
feixe_nao_prova: It shows one specific distinguisher, on reduced instances. It is not an attack on the full 8-round output, and the public API still passes the state through SHA-256 or SHAKE256. Full diffusion in one round, shown in the section above, does not prevent this probe.
sent_intro: v5.2 runs two independent streams, A and B, through all the rounds and compares the two states at the end. If they diverge, it zeroes the output and raises the alarm. Inject a fault and see what the redundancy catches and what it does not.
sent_c_a: Fault in stream A only (what v5.2 detects)
sent_c_antes: Fault in the state before copying (limit)
sent_rodada: Round at which the fault enters
sent_d_a: The reference core injects the fault in stream A only, at the entry of the chosen round. At any round, the final comparison must raise the alarm.
sent_d_ambos: Didactic scenario built here: the same fault enters both streams at once. No temporal redundancy tells this apart from a legitimate input.
sent_d_antes: Didactic scenario built here: the fault corrupts the state before it is copied into A and B. Both streams compute the same wrong result.
sent_alarme_det: The output was zeroed (rc = −2). The two final states differ in {palavras} words and {bits} bits.
sent_saida_errada: The two streams agree, but the delivered output differs from the correct one in {bits} bits. The redundancy did not see the fault.
sent_saida_igual: The output matches the correct one.
sent_limite: Redundancy protects against a transient fault that hits one stream only. It does not protect against a repeatable fault identical in both streams, nor against a fault in shared data (the input, the round keys and the constants), nor against state corrupted between two calls.
kat_intro: Frozen v5.2 vectors. The laboratory recomputes each one now and compares it with the recorded value. The seal only says "equal to the vector", never "secure".
kat_adulterar: Tamper with 1 character of the expected value
kat_selo_nota: Tamper with one character and watch the seal fail: the check detects the change. "Equal to the vector" means this engine agrees with Python and the C core, not that the construction is secure.
cercos_intro: The 9 findings of the internal offensive review, with their status in each version. The ones with a button can be redone here. The others say clearly that they are not recomputed in the browser.
cerco_ir_sent: Run in the Two sentinels section: fault in stream A, round {r}.
cerco_subchave: In {difs} of {total} round keys, the first 16 words of rk[r] differ from K_r. In v5.1 they were a literal copy.
cerco_msb: In {n} random valid inputs, the top bit of words 15 and 31 lit up in {a}. After round 1, word 15 has that bit set in {b} of {n}: the bias disappears.
cerco_somas: The 32 MDS rows have {distintas} distinct XOR sum, with value {valor}. The constant of each round is added identically to the 32 words (one value per round).
lab_nao_6: The dual-key module, the boomerang and the impossible differential are not in this laboratory.
lab_nao_7: The engine is JavaScript with tables: it has no constant time and does not replace the C core.
lab_nao_8: The beam mission uses reduced instances, not the 8-round API.
lab_pontuacao: The laboratory has no score that measures security. Only the guess keeps an average error, in this browser.
feixe_distintos: Distinct values per output word: at least {min} of 65,536; {perm} of the 32 output words are permutations of the beam (65,536 distinct).
feixe_distintos_nota: In 1 round, every output word is a permutation of the beam, and the sum is zero by construction. In 2 rounds the output is no longer a permutation, but it is a linear combination of words that still are permutations (the inputs of the last S-box), and the linear layer preserves the zero sum. From 3 rounds on this stops holding and the sum no longer vanishes. The mosaic shows 2 real bits of the output of each of the 65,536 values.
